question: How many total Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted at the United Nations Sustainable Development Summit in New York in September 2015?
solution:
The correct answer is __**17**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** were adopted at the **United Nations Sustainable Development Summit**, held in **New York** in **September 2015**.
 
• The SDGs are also referred to as the **Global Goals**. They are a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that all people enjoy peace and prosperity by the year **2030**.
 
• There are a total of **17 SDGs**, which address a wide range of global challenges, including **poverty, inequality, climate change, environmental degradation, peace, and justice**. *Hence, the correct option is 17.*
 
• Each goal has specific **targets** to be achieved, with a total of **169 targets** across all the goals, making them comprehensive and interconnected in nature.
 
• The SDGs succeeded the **Millennium Development Goals (MDGs)**, which were in place from **2000 to 2015**. The SDGs were designed to be more inclusive and detailed compared to the MDGs.
 
• The SDGs emphasize collaboration among governments, international organizations, and global stakeholders to achieve sustainable development worldwide.
 
• The **17 SDGs** include goals like **No Poverty**, **Zero Hunger**, **Quality Education**, **Gender Equality**, **Climate Action**, and **Partnerships for the Goals**, among others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The 17 Sustainable Development Goals:**

 
 
• **Goal 1:** No Poverty – Focuses on ending poverty in all its forms everywhere.
 
• **Goal 2:** Zero Hunger – Aims to end hunger, achieve food security, improve nutrition, and promote sustainable agriculture.
 
• **Goal 3:** Good Health and Well-being – Ensures healthy lives and promotes well-being for all at all ages.
 
• **Goal 4:** Quality Education – Ensures inclusive and equitable quality education and promotes lifelong learning opportunities for all.
 
• **Goal 5:** Gender Equality – Achieves gender equality and empowers all women and girls.
 
• **Goal 6:** Clean Water and Sanitation – Ensures availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.
 
• **Goal 7:** Affordable and Clean Energy – Ensures access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all.
 
• **Goal 8:** Decent Work and Economic Growth – Promotes sustained, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment, and decent work for all.
 
• **Goal 9:** Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure – Builds resilient infrastructure, promotes inclusive and sustainable industrialization, and fosters innovation.
 
• **Goal 10:** Reduced Inequalities – Reduces inequality within and among countries.
 
• **Goal 11:** Sustainable Cities and Communities – Makes cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable.
 
• **Goal 12:** Responsible Consumption and Production – Ensures sustainable consumption and production patterns.
 
• **Goal 13:** Climate Action – Takes urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.
 
• **Goal 14:** Life Below Water – Conserves and sustainably uses the oceans, seas, and marine resources.
 
• **Goal 15:** Life on Land – Protects, restores, and promotes sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, manages forests, combats desertification, and halts biodiversity loss.
 
• **Goal 16:** Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions – Promotes peaceful and inclusive societies, provides access to justice for all, and builds effective, accountable institutions.
 
• **Goal 17:** Partnerships for the Goals – Strengthens the means of implementation and revitalizes the global partnership for sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **Importance of SDGs:**
 
 
• The SDGs are crucial for addressing the global challenges that include poverty, inequality, climate change, and environmental degradation.
 
• They are a part of the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**, which was adopted by all United Nations Member States in **2015**.
 
• The SDGs call for a collaborative approach where nations, private sectors, and civil society work together to achieve global sustainable development.
